full_app_parameter_taxonomy.rationale: Exact IUPAC average isotopic residue mass sum + 18.01528 Da (H2O). Zero free parameters; exact to 0.01 Da for both natural and AI-designed polypeptides.
Exact Henderson-Hasselbalch bisection with Bjellqvist et al. (1993, 1994) pKa constants matching ExPASy ProtParam. Not trained on a corpus.
Exact Pace et al. (1995) Beer-Lambert sum (5500*nW + 1490*nY + 125*nSS). Zero-Trp/Tyr AI designs are handled via explicit UV-280 blindness warnings (214/205 nm), not retraining.
Kyte & Doolittle (1982) hydropathy average and Ikai (1980) aliphatic index; standardized definitions with zero local training.

Guruprasad (1990) 400-dipeptide DIWV table (44 proteins) and Wilkinson-Harrison/Davis (1991/1999) 2-term discriminant (81 E. coli proteins). Modifying weights would break ExPASy ProtParam parity; instead, Glu/Lys-rich de novo caveats are surfaced directly in workflow alerts.

Exact m = C*V*MW and V_liq = m/rho stoichiometry, IUPAC formula weights, Cytiva CIPP chromatography rules, and UniProt ChEBI/keyword guards. AI-designed edge cases (2KL8, 6D0T, 6X1K, zero-A280, Glu/Lys II) are solved deterministically by biophysical rules.

full_app_parameter_taxonomy.category: Low-DOF Calibrated Physical Hydrodynamics & Pore Partitioning
full_app_parameter_taxonomy.rationale: 3-coeff quadratic log-MW Rh law (R^2 = 0.9950 across 1,254 PDB assemblies, 55 Cytiva calibration standards, MAE 0.17-0.22 mL) + 2-parameter Ackers erfc pore integral per column + Uversky (2002) coil + Tirado-Garcia de la Torre DNA rod equations. Already constrained below column-to-column variance (~0.2 mL); 10x more points cannot reduce physical shape/hydration variance.
3-parameter Ferguson / Ogston-Rodbard-Chrambach sigmoidal sieving curve calibrated to Bio-Rad Precision Plus Dual Color markers across 4%-22% polyacrylamide.
Exact C1*V1 = C2*V2 volumetric dilution with volume conservation (Sambrook/Bio-Rad Laemmli & Schagger 2006 Tricine). Zero learned parameters.
Deterministic helix/strand/coil parametric geometry and exact PDB/mmCIF parser (AlphaFold2/ESMFold/RFdiffusion/X-ray). Zero learned parameters.
Exact NCBI Standard Genetic Code (transl_table=1, 64 codons) and deterministic API/regex resolution.

full_app_parameter_taxonomy.category: Locally Machine-Learned Single-Sequence Neural Model (1,138,586 params)
full_app_parameter_taxonomy.rationale: THE ONLY machine-learned model in ProPurify Studio (currently trained on 3,751 PDB/DSSP chains out of 14,869 in data/ss_10k_corpus.npz). Evaluated empirically via controlled zero-leakage learning curve (N = 500 -> 1,000 -> 3,751 -> 7,500 -> 11,230) + 2x-width capacity ablation + power-law extrapolation to 10x (37,510 chains).

mathematical_extrapolation_to_10x.single_sequence_information_ceiling_note: Classic single-sequence 3-state secondary structure prediction (without evolutionary MSAs/PSSMs or multi-hundred-million-parameter pLMs like ESM-2) has a well-established biophysical information ceiling near ~70-72% Q3 because ~25-30% of residue SS assignments depend on long-range tertiary contacts (beta-sheet pairing partners 50-200 residues apart). Our empirical zero-leakage curve confirms diminishing returns: +0.90% Q3 for 500->1,000 (2x), +1.72% for 1,000->3,751 (3.75x), collapsing to just +0.19% Q3 (69.15%->69.34%) for 3,751->7,500 (2x) and +0.03% for GOR-IV at 3x (11,230).

engineering_verdict.summary: NO — increasing training size 10x across all parameters is NOT needed and NOT recommended: (1) 11 of 12 parameter families across ProPurify Studio are exact closed-form physics/chemistry formulas, low-DOF calibrated physical laws (SEC R^2=0.9950, MAE 0.17-0.22 mL; SDS-PAGE Ferguson Rf), fixed literature scales (ExPASy ProtParam parity), or deterministic rules — '10x training data' does not apply to them. (2) For the sole ML model (modules/secondary_structure.py, 1.14M params, 4.04 MB, ~20 ms/protein), our strictly zero-leakage controlled learning curve (3,639 homology-disjoint natural test chains + 32 real experimental AI-designed PDBs) proves asymptotic saturation: doubling training chains from 3,751 (1.45M res) to 7,500 (2.80M res) improves natural pooled Q3 by only +0.19% (69.15% -> 69.34%), SOV_99 by +0.32% (59.26% -> 59.58%), Mean MCC by +0.0014 (0.4987 -> 0.5001), and GOR-IV at 3x (11,230 chains) gains only +0.03% (61.31% -> 61.34%). Power-law saturation (R^2=0.9878) projects 10x data (37,510 chains) would add only +1.03% Q3 (to ~70.18%, local log-linear bound ~69.78%, asymptotic ceiling ~70.99%), which is well below a meaningful +1.5-2.0% jump while destroying the strict >=10,500-protein held-out zero-leakage test benchmark if drawn from the local corpus. (3) Keeping current ss_model_weights.npz (3,751 train / 11,118 test) preserves zero-leakage benchmark integrity, 4.04 MB footprint, <21 ms CPU latency, and already achieves 80.91% Q3 / 80.92% SOV_99 / 93.8% fold-class accuracy on AI-designed proteins. Breaking past ~72% Q3 in a future release would require an architectural paradigm shift (MSA/PSSM profiles or a pretrained pLM like ESM-2), not 10x more single-sequence training rows.
